items.name: Conjecture 1.1 (Colliot-Thélène): Brauer–Manin density for rationally connected varieties
items.statement: For any smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible, rationally connected variety X over a number field k, the set X(k) is dense in X(A_k)^{Br(X)}.
items.locator: Conjecture 1.1, p. 1 (author final version (= arXiv v4))
items.note: A conjecture, recorded as a statement and never used as a hypothesis-free theorem. HW20 (unreviewed) routed the same statement, its item 133, to HeightsRationalPointsPartIIHomogeneousMassey. The fibration theorems here are its main consumers, so this extraction proposes the zero-cycle/fibration Part II as its single owner (see the report).

items.name: Adelic points and the Brauer–Manin set
items.statement: X(A_k) = ∏'_v X(k_v) (restricted product with respect to an integral model), and X(A_k)^{Br(X)} ⊆ X(A_k) is the set of adelic points (x_v) with Σ_v inv_v β(x_v) = 0 for all β ∈ Br(X). It is closed and contains the image of X(k), by global reciprocity.
items.note: RP.2 plans restricted adelic point spaces, local invariants and the Brauer–Manin pairing with its finite-support theorem.
items.apiStatus: open: consumer-derived planning API and three discriminating tests required; see G2

items.name: The Brauer pairing on zero-cycles
items.statement: For a variety X over a field k, ⟨−,−⟩ : Br(X) × Z_0(X) → Br(k) is characterised by ⟨β, P⟩ = Cores_{k(P)/k}(β(P)) for a closed point P. If X is proper it factors through rational equivalence, giving Br(X) × CH_0(X) → Br(k) (Manin, Définition 7 and Proposition 8). Over a number field, summing local invariants gives Br(X) × Z_{0,A}(X) → Q/Z (1.4) and, for smooth proper X, Br(X) × ĈH_{0,A}(X) → Q/Z (1.5).
items.note: HW20 routed the cycle version of the Brauer evaluation interface as a source of RP.2, and this item follows it. The factorisation through rational equivalence needs properness.
items.apiStatus: open: consumer-derived planning API and three discriminating tests required; see G2

items.name: The modified adelic Chow group CH_{0,A}(X), completions, and the complex (E)
items.statement: For smooth proper X over a number field k, CH_{0,A}(X) = ∏_{v∈Ω_f} CH_0(X⊗k_v) × ∏_{v∈Ω_∞} CH_0(X⊗k_v)/N_{k̄_v/k_v}(CH_0(X⊗k̄_v)). For an abelian group M, M̂ = lim_n M/nM. The complex (E) is ĈH_0(X) → ĈH_{0,A}(X) → Hom(Br(X), Q/Z), the second map being Σ_v ⟨−,−⟩_v. It is a complex by global reciprocity. Z_{0,A}(X) is the set of families (z_v) whose supports are integral over O_v for almost all v with respect to a model.
items.note: HW20 items 24 and 27 (modified local Chow groups, exactness property (E)) are routed to the same Part II. SF.5 supplies CH_0 and proper pushforward.

items.name: Conjecture 1.2 (Colliot-Thélène–Sansuc, Kato–Saito), in van Hamel's formulation
items.statement: For any smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible variety X over a number field k, the complex (E) is exact.
items.note: A conjecture, recorded as a statement. Rationally connected varieties that satisfy Conjecture 1.1 over every finite extension of k satisfy it (Liang).

items.name: Definition 1.7: properties (E) and (E₁)
items.statement: A smooth proper variety X over a number field k satisfies (E) if (E) is exact. It satisfies (E₁) if the existence of (z_v) ∈ ∏_v Z_0(X⊗k_v) orthogonal to Br(X) with deg(z_v) = 1 for all v implies the existence of a zero-cycle of degree 1 on X. (E) implies (E₁).
items.note: Shared with HW20's candidate owner.

items.name: Split varieties, symmetric products and effective reduced cycles over a curve
items.statement: A variety over k is split if it contains a geometrically integral open subset. Sym_{X/k} = ⊔_{d≥1} Sym^d_{X/k} for quasi-projective X. For f : X → C to a smooth proper curve, Z_0^{eff,red}(X) is the set of effective zero-cycles z with f_*z reduced. Over a number field, Z^{eff,red}_{0,A}(X) = Z_{0,A}(X) ∩ ∏_v Z_0^{eff,red}(X⊗k_v). For y ∈ Pic(C), Z^{eff,red,y}_{0,A}(X) consists of families with f_*z_v linearly equivalent to y at finite v, and equivalent up to a norm from k̄_v at infinite v.
items.note: Symmetric powers of a smooth curve are planned in the Jacobian Challenge (Layer C). The adelic effective-reduced sets are specific to the fibration method.

items.name: Hilbert subsets (in Lang's sense, of all scheme points)
items.statement: A subset H of an irreducible variety X is a Hilbert subset if there are a dense open X⁰ ⊆ X, n ≥ 1 and irreducible finite étale X⁰-schemes W_1, …, W_n such that H is the set of points of X⁰ above which every W_i has irreducible fiber. H is not a subset of X(k): the generic point belongs to every Hilbert subset.
items.note: HW20's item 10 records that IG.2 plans Hilbert subsets of all scheme points, and Hilbert irreducibility.

items.name: Strong approximation off a place
items.statement: A variety X over k satisfies strong approximation off v₀ if X(k_{v₀}) = ∅, or if for every finite S ∋ v₀ containing Ω_∞ and every model 𝒳 over 𝒪_S, the diagonal map 𝒳(𝒪_S) → ∏_{v∈S∖{v₀}} X(k_v) × ∏_{v∉S} 𝒳(𝒪_v) has dense image.
items.note: Tau Ceti Global Number Fields Layer 6 plans additive strong approximation (the case of 𝔾_a and the ideles), not this property of varieties.
items.apiStatus: open: consumer-derived planning API and three discriminating tests required; see G2

items.name: Lemma 1.8 (Cao–Xu, Wei): A^n minus codimension 2 satisfies strong approximation
items.statement: Let n ≥ 1, k a number field, v₀ a place of k and F ⊆ A^n_k a closed subset of codimension ≥ 2. Then U = A^n_k ∖ F satisfies strong approximation off v₀. Proof: weakly approximate by Q ∈ U(k), choose Q′ with the line through Q, Q′ inside U, and apply strong approximation off v₀ on that line.
items.note: Imports weak approximation and additive strong approximation (Tau Ceti Global Number Fields Layers 1 and 6). The general-line step uses codim F ≥ 2.

items.name: Theorem 1.3: the fibration theorem for zero-cycles over P^1
items.statement: Let X be a smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible variety over a number field k and f : X → P^1_k a dominant morphism with rationally connected geometric generic fiber. If the smooth fibers of f satisfy Conjecture 1.2, so does X.
items.note: The special case of Theorem 8.3(1) with C = P^1 (item 52).

items.name: Theorem 1.4: fibrations into homogeneous spaces satisfy (E)
items.statement: Let X be smooth, proper, irreducible over k; Y irreducible, birational to P^n, C or P^n × C (n ≥ 1, C a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve satisfying (E)); f : X → Y dominant with generic fiber birational to a homogeneous space of a connected linear algebraic group with connected geometric stabilisers. Then X satisfies (E).
items.note: Restated as Corollary 8.5 (item 58).

items.name: Theorem 1.5: the conditional fibration theorem for rational points
items.statement: Let X be smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible over k and f : X → P^1_k dominant with rationally connected geometric generic fiber. Assume Conjecture 9.1. If the smooth fibers of f above rational points satisfy Conjecture 1.1, so does X.
items.note: The case n = 1 of Corollary 9.25 (item 92).

items.name: Theorem 1.6: the unconditional fibration theorem over Q (via Matthiesen)
items.statement: Let X be smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible over Q and f : X → P^1_Q dominant with rationally connected geometric generic fiber, whose non-split fibers all lie over rational points. If X_c(Q) is dense in X_c(A_Q)^{Br(X_c)} for every rational point c of a Hilbert subset of P^1_Q, then X(Q) is dense in X(A_Q)^{Br(X)}.
items.note: Restated as Theorem 9.28 (item 94).

items.name: Zero-cycles on norm hypersurfaces N_{K/k}(x) = P(t)
items.statement: For any finite extension K/k of number fields (or any finite extension K/k(t)) and any nonzero P(t) ∈ k[t], a smooth proper model of N_{K/k}(x_1ω_1 + ⋯ + x_nω_n) = P(t) satisfies (E). The generic fiber over the t-line is a torsor under the norm torus, and smooth compactifications of torsors under tori satisfy Conjecture 1.1.
items.locator: §1, (1.3) and the discussion after it, pp. 2–3
items.note: An application of Theorem 1.3 in its form Corollary 8.4(2) (item 57), using Sansuc's theorem for tori (item 59) and Lemma 8.2.

items.name: Definition 2.1: the groups Pic₊(C) and Br₊(C)
items.statement: Let C be a smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curve over a field k of characteristic 0, C⁰ = C ∖ M dense open, and for m ∈ M a nonzero finite étale k(m)-algebra L_m. Pic₊(C) is Div(C⁰) modulo div(f) for those f invertible at every m ∈ M with f(m) ∈ N_{L_m/k(m)}(L_m^*). Br₊(C) ⊆ Br(C⁰) is the set of classes whose residue at each m ∈ M lies in Ker(r_m : H¹(k(m), Q/Z) → H¹(L_m, Q/Z)). There are exact sequences k^* → ⊕_m k(m)^*/N(L_m^*) → Pic₊(C) → Pic(C) → 0 and 0 → Br(C) → Br₊(C) → ⊕_m Ker(r_m) → H³(C, 𝔾_m). In particular Br₊(C)/Br(C) is finite.
items.note: Pic₊(C) is a quotient of Rosenlicht's relative Picard group Pic(C, M). The finiteness of Br₊(C)/Br(C) is what makes the formal lemma applicable.
items.apiStatus: open: consumer-derived planning API and three discriminating tests required; see G2

items.name: Proposition 2.3: hypercohomological description of Pic₊ and Br₊
items.statement: With 𝓔 = τ_{≤1}Rρ_*[j_*𝔾_m → ⊕_m i_{m*}ℤ], there are canonical isomorphisms Pic₊(C) = H⁰(k, RHom(𝓔, 𝔾_m)) and Br₊(C) = H²(k, 𝓔).
items.note: Uses Deligne's universal coefficient formula. SF.2 supplies étale cohomology of schemes.

items.name: Proposition 2.4 and the adelic complex for Pic₊
items.statement: The pairing Br(C⁰) × Div(C⁰) → Br(k) induces Br₊(C) × Pic₊(C) → Br(k). Over a number field, summing local invariants gives Br₊(C) × Pic₊,A(C) → Q/Z, where Pic₊,A(C) is the restricted product of the Pic₊(C⊗k_v) (modified by norms at infinite places). Global reciprocity makes Pic₊(C) → Pic₊,A(C) → Hom(Br₊(C), Q/Z) a complex. It is not exact in general when C has positive genus.

items.name: Theorem 2.5 (Wittenberg, Corollaire 5.7): arithmetic duality for Pic₊
items.statement: Any element of Pic₊,A(C) that is orthogonal to Br₊(C) and whose image in Pic_A(C) comes from Pic(C) is the image of an element of Pic₊(C).
items.note: When C = P^1 this is Poitou–Tate duality for the norm-one tori of the L_m/k(m) (item 20). For positive genus its proof needs the hypercohomological formalism of [Wit12, §5].

items.name: Poitou–Tate duality for tori
items.statement: For a torus T over a number field k with character lattice T̂, the Tate–Shafarevich kernels Sha¹(k,T) and Sha²(k,T̂) are dual. The image of H¹(k,T) in the sum of the local H¹(k_v,T) is the orthogonal of the diagonal H¹(k,T̂), for the sum of the local cup/invariant pairings. In Sha² the localization maps H²(k,T̂)→H²(k_v,T̂) must be explicit; the whole H² group is not its kernel.
items.note: R02.4 plans Poitou–Tate duality with its lattice versions. HW20 routed the torus/character-lattice statements to it as a source.

items.name: Harari's formal lemma and ramified-evaluation theorem
items.statement: (a) Let X⁰ ⊆ X be a dense open subset of a smooth variety over a number field and B ⊂ Br(X⁰) finite. Then adelic points of X⁰ orthogonal to B are dense in the set of adelic points of X orthogonal to B ∩ Br(X) (Harari, Corollaire 2.6.1). (b) If β ∈ Br(X⁰) ∖ Br(X), then β(a) ≠ 0 for some a ∈ X⁰(k_v), for infinitely many places v (Théorème 2.1.1). (c) If β ∈ Br(f^{-1}(𝒰)) and x ∈ X(k_v) specialises to a smooth point of a split fiber component Y, then inv_v β(x) = n·∂_{β,Y}(Frob), with n the local intersection multiplicity (Corollaire 2.4.3).
items.locator: §3 introduction, proofs of Lemma 3.3, Theorem 9.17, Lemma 9.20, pp. 11–12 and 43–46
items.note: HW20 routed the formal lemma as a source of RP.2, and this item follows it. These are the core Brauer-evaluation inputs of every fibration argument. Independent review: Part (c) is only the good-model evaluation formula used on author pp44–46: enlarge S so the residue covers and smooth component models extend, the relevant torsion is invertible, and the point meets the chosen component in the prescribed transverse/intersection-multiplicity setting. The generic sentence does not provide all Har94 hypotheses; split these three inputs and acquire the original source before route1 is accepted.

items.name: Proposition 3.1: the formal lemma for effective reduced zero-cycles in a fixed class
items.statement: Let C be a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve of genus g over a number field k, y ∈ Pic(C) with deg(y) > 2g + 1, X smooth irreducible and f : X → C with geometrically irreducible generic fiber, X⁰ ⊆ X dense open and B ⊂ Br(X⁰) finite. For any (z_v) ∈ Z^{eff,red,y}_{0,A}(X⁰) orthogonal to B ∩ Br(X) and any finite S ⊂ Ω, there is (z′_v) ∈ Z^{eff,red,y}_{0,A}(X⁰) orthogonal to B with z′_v = z_v for v ∈ S.
items.note: Lemma 3.2 lifts classes of degree > 2g to effective reduced cycles integral outside S′, using the moving lemma [Wit12, Lemme 4.2], Lang–Weil–Nisnevich and Hensel. Lemma 3.3 is the cycle analogue of item 21(b). The proof then repeats Harari's Pontryagin-duality argument.

items.name: Moving lemmas for zero-cycles on curves in the total space
items.statement: (a) Wittenberg12 Lemma4.2: let R be a henselian local domain with infinite fraction field K and residue field F, let C/R be a smooth projective curve of genus g, and M a proper closed subset of its generic fibre. If #F≥deg(M), every divisor D of degree>2g is linearly equivalent to a reduced effective divisor of smooth support whose closure avoids the closure of M. This moves divisors on the base curve; lifting to X is the separate good-place statement HW16 Lemma3.2, requiring enlargement of the exceptional set and Lang–Weil/Hensel. (b) In the smooth proper fibration setup of HW16 Proposition7.5, the cited Bertini/moving suppliers choose local smooth proper geometrically integral curves through prescribed finite supports and a chosen closed point, dominating C; sufficiently large additions of that point can be made effective with reduced pushforward.
items.locator: HW16 author pp11,24; Wittenberg12 author pp21–22, Lemmas4.2–4.3 (statement and proof of4.2 read independently).
items.note: Corrects a false universal lifting claim and a wrong use of the Wit12 locator. Original CT00 and Wit12 Lemma4.4 remain separate source-acquisition obligations.

items.name: Lang–Weil–Nisnevich estimates
items.statement: A geometrically irreducible variety of dimension d over F_q has q^d + O(q^{d−1/2}) rational points, the constant depending only on the geometry of an embedding. In particular smooth geometrically irreducible fibers over closed points of large residue characteristic have rational points, which Hensel's lemma lifts.
items.note: WeilConjectures WC.5 plans point-count bounds for smooth projective varieties from cohomology. The elementary Lang–Weil estimate for arbitrary geometrically irreducible varieties is not stated anywhere in the atlas.

items.name: Formally smooth algebra lifting to an adically complete ring
items.statement: Let R,A,S be commutative rings with R-algebra structures on A and S, assume A formally smooth over R, and let I be an ideal of S with S I-adically complete. Every R-algebra map A→S/I lifts to an R-algebra map A→S whose composite with the quotient is the original map.
items.note: Exact pinned algebra theorem read with its surrounding variables. The scheme-level Hensel consequence is separated as item100; the cited declaration alone does not construct the affine-chart and scheme-smoothness comparison.

items.name: Proposition 4.1 (Harari): specialisation of the Brauer group over a Hilbert subset
items.statement: Let C be a smooth irreducible curve over a number field k and f : X → C with smooth, proper, irreducible geometric generic fiber X_η̄ satisfying H¹(X_η̄, Q/Z) = 0 and H²(X_η̄, 𝒪) = 0. Let C⁰ ⊆ C be dense open, X⁰ = f^{-1}(C⁰) and B ⊆ Br(X⁰). If B → Br(X_η)/f_η^*Br(η) is surjective, there is a Hilbert subset H ⊆ C⁰ such that B → Br(X_h)/f_h^*Br(h) is surjective for all h ∈ H.
items.note: Proof: Gal(η̄/η) acts on H²(X_η̄, Q/Z(1)) through a finite quotient (Br(X_η̄) finite, NS finitely generated). Hilbert irreducibility for the corresponding Galois cover makes γ_h an isomorphism, and Hochschild–Serre with H³(k(C), Q/Z(1)) = 0 concludes. Remark 4.4: the same holds over any base when H³(η) → H³(X_η) is injective. Independent review: X is irreducible and f dominant in the source setup; keep these hypotheses, the geometric generic fibre and the characteristic-zero number field explicit. Separate Lemmas4.2–4.3 and their original finiteness suppliers before proof closure.

items.name: Vanishing of H³(k(C), Q/Z(1)) for a curve over a number field
items.statement: For a curve C over a number field k, H³(k(C), Q/Z(1)) = 0 (Colliot-Thélène–Poonen, Lemma 2.6; equivalently H³(k(C), 𝔾_m) = 0).
items.note: A cited input of the specialisation argument.

items.name: Grothendieck's Kummer sequence for Br and finiteness of geometric Br
items.statement: For a smooth variety X over a characteristic-zero field (étale cohomology): 0 → Pic(X) ⊗ Q/Z → H²(X, Q/Z(1)) → Br(X) → 0. If X is smooth proper over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 with H²(X, 𝒪_X) = 0, then Br(X) is finite, and H²(X, Q/Z(1)) is an extension of Br(X) by NS(X) ⊗ Q/Z.
items.locator: proof of Proposition 4.1 and Lemma 4.2, pp. 12–13
items.note: Belongs to the scheme-cohomology foundation (étale 𝔾_m cohomology), which HW20 also routed to SF.2. In positive characteristic only prime-to-characteristic torsion is covered by this étale Kummer formulation; fppf p-primary coefficients require a separate comparison.

items.name: Smooth and proper base change for étale cohomology
items.statement: For a smooth proper morphism of finite presentation, with finite locally constant torsion coefficients of order invertible on the base, higher direct images are locally constant with finite stalks and the base-change maps identify geometric fibre cohomology. Over a characteristic-zero field take the filtered colimit to Q/Z(j). Comparisons between geometric fibres use étale paths, with the corresponding fundamental-group transport; a path-independent identification is not asserted.
items.locator: proof of Lemma 4.3 and Lemma 8.10, pp. 13 and 31
items.note: SF.2 plans proper and smooth base change.

items.name: The Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence for a variety over a field
items.statement: For a variety X over a field k, geometric base change to a separable closure, and an étale abelian coefficient sheaf M with its descent data, the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence H^p(G_k,H^q(X_ksep,M))⇒H^(p+q)(X,M) has the natural low-degree edge maps. The paper uses characteristic-zero fields and the G_m/torsion comparison. Import the group spectral sequence from R02.2 and construct the scheme comparison in SF.2.
items.note: R02.2 (Hochschild–Serre and descent) plans the group-theoretic version. HW23's accepted source route adds the scheme-theoretic edge sequence to SF.2.

items.name: Theorem 5.1: existence of zero-cycles on fibrations over curves
items.statement: Let C be a smooth projective geometrically irreducible curve over a number field k, X smooth projective irreducible, f : X → C with geometrically irreducible generic fiber and no multiple fiber, C⁰ ⊆ C dense open over which f is smooth, X⁰ = f^{-1}(C⁰), B ⊂ Br(X⁰) finite, y ∈ Pic(C), (z_v) ∈ Z^{eff,red,y}_{0,A}(X⁰), S ⊂ Ω_f finite and 𝒰 a neighbourhood of (z_v)_{v∈S} in ∏_{v∈S} Sym_{X⁰/k}(k_v). Assume (i) (z_v) is orthogonal to (B + f_η^*Br(η)) ∩ Br(X); (ii) deg(y) ≥ deg(M) + 2g + 2 (M = C ∖ C⁰); (iii) at each real v, Supp(z_v) lies on a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve Z_v ⊂ X⊗k_v dominating C with deg(y) ≥ [k_v(Z_v):k_v(C)]deg(M) + 2g_v + 2. Then there are (z′_v) ∈ Z_{0,A}(X⁰) and an effective divisor c on C⁰ of class y with (1) f_*z′_v = c for all v; (2) (z′_v) orthogonal to B; (3) z′_v effective for v ∈ S and (z′_v)_{v∈S} ∈ 𝒰; (4) at each real v, z_v − z′_v has even total coefficient on each connected component of X⁰(k_v). If every fiber has a component of multiplicity 1, all z′_v can be taken effective.
items.note: The core existence theorem. It replaces Dirichlet's theorem, and so needs no abelianness hypothesis. Independent review: No multiple fibre means that the gcd of the geometric component multiplicities is1; this is weaker than the existence of a component of multiplicity1. Do not replace one hypothesis by the other.

items.name: Lemma 5.2: elements with locally split divisors from strong approximation
items.statement: Let L/k be a finite extension of number fields, S a finite set of places and t_v ∈ k_v^* (v ∈ S) norms from (L⊗k_v)^*. There is t ∈ k^*, arbitrarily close to t_v for v ∈ S, such that at every finite v ∉ S either t is a unit or L has a place of degree 1 over v. Given a place v₀ ∉ S over which L has a place of degree 1, t can be taken integral outside S ∪ {v₀}.
items.note: Proof: apply Lemma 1.8 to W = R_{L/k}(A¹) ∖ F, F the singular locus of the complement of R_{L/k}𝔾_m, and take t = N_{L/k}(x). The components of D ∖ F are permuted like the embeddings of L, so a k_v-point of D ∖ F embeds L into k_v. Uses Weil restriction (item 40) and Chebotarev (item 98).

items.name: Lemma 5.3: Br₊ controls the vertical part
items.statement: (B + f_η^*Br(η)) ∩ Br(X) ⊆ B + f^*Br₊(C), and ((B + f_η^*Br(η)) ∩ Br(X))/f^*Br(C) is finite (C, M, L_m built from residues of B along fiber components, L_m Galois containing the algebraic closures L_{m,i} of k(m) in the extensions E_{m,i} killing those residues).
items.note: Uses the residue formula of item 34 and gcd(e_{m,i}) = 1 (no multiple fibers).

items.name: Residues of pulled-back Brauer classes
items.statement: If γ ∈ Br(k(C)) has residue ∂_γ ∈ H¹(k(m), Q/Z) at m and Y is a component of multiplicity e of f^{-1}(m), the residue of f^*γ at the generic point of Y is e·Res(∂_γ) in H¹(k(Y), Q/Z) (Colliot-Thélène–Swinnerton-Dyer, Proposition 1.1.1). Purity: a class on a regular scheme that is unramified along every divisor extends.
items.locator: proof of Lemma 5.3, p. 16; proof of Lemma 5.9; Proposition 9.9
items.note: Residue maps and purity for Brauer groups belong to the scheme-cohomology foundation. HW20 routed its residue and purity items as a source of SF.2.

items.name: Lemmas 5.4–5.6: approximation at S and at the infinite places
items.statement: (5.4) One can replace (z_v) by a family orthogonal to B + f^*Br₊(C) (Proposition 3.1 with a finite Λ ⊂ Br₊(C), Br₊ = Λ + Br(C)). (5.5) At each infinite v there are h_v ∈ H⁰(C⊗k_v, 𝒪(c₁)) and z_v² ∈ Z^{eff,red,y}_0(X⁰⊗k_v) with div(h_v) = f_*z_v² − c₁, h_v(m) a norm from L_m⊗k_v, and z_v − z_v² of even total coefficient on each connected component of X⁰(k_v). (5.6) By the inverse function theorem for the smooth map f_* : Sym_{X⁰} → Sym_{C⁰} at reduced divisors, c lifts near (z_v)_{v∈S} and (z_v²)_{v real}.
items.note: Lemma 5.5 uses Serre duality on Z_v, H¹(Z_v, 𝒪(z_v¹ − M_v)) = 0, and the sign-change count of a real rational function.

items.name: Construction of c₁, v₀ and the divisor c
items.statement: By Theorem 2.5 there is c₁ ∈ Div(C⁰) of class y whose class in Pic₊,A(C) equals that of (f_*z_v). Fix v₀ ∉ S split completely in all L_m. For each m, Lemma 5.2 gives t_m ∈ k(m)^* close to h_v(m) at S ∪ Ω_∞, integral away from S ∪ {v₀}, with divisor supported on places above S or split in L_m. Since deg(y) ≥ deg(M) + 2g + 2, H¹(𝒞, 𝒪(c̃₁ − M̃)) = 0, so H⁰(𝒞, 𝒪(c̃₁)) → H⁰(M̃, 𝒪) is a split surjection of free 𝒪_S-modules. Strong approximation off v₀ in its kernel gives h ∈ H⁰(C, 𝒪(c₁)) with h(m) = t_m, close to h_v at S ∪ Ω_∞, with no pole outside Supp(c̃₁) ∪ 𝒞_{v₀}. Then c = c₁ + div(h).
items.note: Remark 9.12 rephrases the construction as strong approximation on an auxiliary variety W. Independent review: Enlarge S to kill the class group of O_S before asserting that the relevant finite projective modules are free. Record the chosen integral curve model, Cartier closure of c1, and degree/vanishing hypotheses. Item102 is the needed one-omitted-place approximation supplier, stronger than upstream Layer6’s stated theorem.
items.apiStatus: open: consumer-derived planning API and three discriminating tests required; see G2

items.name: Lemmas 5.7–5.9: local cycles over the degenerate fibers and vanishing evaluations
items.statement: (5.7) Every closed point w ∈ m̃ ∩ Supp(c̃) splits completely in L_m. (5.8) For v ∉ S, m, i, w | v and a rational point ξ of 𝒴_{m̃,i} over w, and a closed point y_v of C⁰⊗k_v whose closure contains w, there is an effective z with f_*z = e_{m,i}y_v whose closure meets the special fiber only at ξ (a finite flat multisection of degree e_{m,i} built from a regular system of parameters). (5.9) For β ∈ B, ⟨β, z′_{v,0}⟩ = 0 and ⟨β, z′_{w,m,i}⟩ = 0, since residues along 𝒴_{m̃,i} die at ξ (the cover ℰ_{m̃,i} has a rational point there) and Br of a complete local ring with finite residue field vanishes.
items.note: Combining the z′_{w,m,i} with Bézout coefficients f_{m,i} (Σ e_{m,i}f_{m,i} = 1) gives f_*z′_v = c.

items.name: Brauer groups of finite 𝒪_v-algebras and complete local rings vanish
items.statement: Br(A) = 0 for any finite 𝒪_v-algebra A, and for any complete (Henselian) local ring with finite residue field (Grothendieck, Brauer III, Proposition 1.5 and Théorème 11.7).
items.note: A scheme-cohomology input that SF.2 should state (Br of Henselian local rings equals Br of the residue field).

items.name: Riemann–Roch vanishing on curves and on their integral models
items.statement: For a smooth proper geometrically connected curve C/k of genus g and a line bundle O(D) with deg D>2g−2, H¹(C,O(D))=0; deg D≥2g gives global generation and deg D≥2g+1 very ampleness. For a smooth proper curve model over O_S and a line bundle of this high degree on every geometric fibre, cohomology and base change gives R¹ρ_*L=0. Apply this to an extended Cartier divisor after enlarging S; the generic-fibre degree alone is not an unspecified-model hypothesis.
items.note: Serre duality and Riemann–Roch: Jacobian Challenge Layer B. Cohomology and base change: Layer C.

items.name: Affine Weil restriction and the norm map
items.statement: For a finite separable field extension L/k, construct Res_(L/k) A¹ and Res_(L/k) G_m and the norm map, with the splitting-field product description and functorial base change. For finite locally free integral models use the same affine representability construction; smooth normal-crossings boundary geometry requires the additional étale condition recorded in103.
items.note: RG2.0a explicitly owns the carrier and norm. Boundary geometry is separated into103 to avoid claiming it is already named by that stage.
items.apiStatus: open: consumer-derived planning API and three discriminating tests required; see G2

items.name: Symmetric powers of smooth projective curves
items.statement: For a smooth projective curve C/k construct Sym^d(C) as a smooth projective scheme representing relative effective divisors of degree d, with base-change and divisor/Picard maps. General quasi-projective X and smoothness of Sym^d(f) at reduced-image cycles are the additional item101.
items.locator: Notation and conventions; Lemma 5.6, pp. 6 and 18
items.note: JacobianChallenge LayerC supplies precisely the curve carrier; it does not already plan every quasi-projective quotient and its fibration smoothness theorem.

items.name: Lemma 6.1 (after Swinnerton-Dyer/Smeets): Hilbert subsets are open near a closed point
items.statement: Let V be normal quasi-projective over a number field, H ⊆ V a Hilbert subset and h ∈ H a closed point. For every finite S there are a finite T disjoint from S and a neighbourhood 𝒱 of h in ∏_{v∈T} Sym_{V/k}(k_v) such that every effective zero-cycle in Sym_{V/k}(k) ∩ 𝒱 is a closed point of V lying in H.
items.note: Extends Smeets' Proposition 6.1 from rational points to closed points, through the universal family of reduced cycles of degree deg(h).

items.name: Hilbert's irreducibility theorem
items.statement: For an irreducible finite étale cover of a dense open of P^1_k (k a number field), infinitely many rational points have irreducible fiber. Hilbert subsets of P^1_k contain rational points.
items.locator: proofs of Theorems 6.2 and 9.22, pp. 21 and 46
items.note: IG.2 plans Hilbert irreducibility over number fields.

items.name: Theorem 6.2: Theorem 5.1 with c a closed point of a given Hilbert subset
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Theorem 5.1, for any Hilbert subset H ⊆ C, the divisor c can be required to be a closed point of C belonging to H.
items.note: Proof: a finite map π : C → P^1 with fibers in |y| and Hilbert irreducibility give a closed point h ∈ H of class y. Then (z_v) is modified at places T from Lemma 6.1 to lie over h, and Theorem 5.1 is applied.

items.name: Theorem 7.1: from completed adelic Chow groups to effective cycles
items.statement: Let f : X → C be as in Theorem 5.1 with X_η̄ irreducible, H¹(X_η̄, Q/Z) = 0 and A₀(X_η̄⊗K) = 0 (K an algebraic closure of k(X_η̄)). Given X⁰ ⊆ X dense open, Φ : ℕ² → ℕ and ẑ_A ∈ ĈH_{0,A}(X) with f_*ẑ_A in the image of P̂ic(C) → P̂ic_A(C), there are y ∈ Pic(C), ẑ ∈ ĈH_0(X), z^eff_A = (z_v) ∈ Z^{eff,red,y}_{0,A}(X⁰), a finite S ⊂ Ω_f and a neighbourhood 𝒰 of (z_v)_{v∈S} with: ẑ_A = z^eff_A + ẑ; at infinite v, Supp(z_v) lies on a smooth proper curve Z_v dominating C with deg(y) ≥ Φ(g_v, d_v); and every z′_A ∈ Z_{0,A}(X⁰) with f_*z′_A ≡ y in Pic_A(C) satisfying (3)–(4) of Theorem 5.1 equals z^eff_A in CH_{0,A}(X).

items.name: Theorem 7.2 (Wittenberg): kernel and cokernel of f_* on CH_0
items.statement: Let f : X → Y be proper dominant between smooth irreducible varieties over k. (i) There is n > 0 with Coker(f_* : CH_0(X⊗k′) → CH_0(Y⊗k′)) killed by n for every extension k′/k. (ii) If X_η̄ is smooth irreducible with A₀(X_η̄⊗K) = 0, some n kills Ker(f_*) for every k′. (iii) If moreover H¹(X_η̄, Q/Z) = 0, Y is a proper curve and k a number field, then f_* : CH_0(X⊗k_v) → CH_0(Y⊗k_v) is an isomorphism for almost all v.
items.note: Relies on a relative decomposition of the diagonal and on Kato–Saito–Sato for Chow groups over finite and local fields. HW20's item 28 is its rationally connected specialisation in the same Part II.

items.name: Lemma 7.3: completions of abelian groups
items.statement: Let h : A → B have cokernel of finite exponent. (i) Coker(h) → Coker(ĥ) is injective. (ii) If B[N] is finite for all N, then the completion of Ker(h) surjects onto Ker(ĥ) and Coker(Ker(h) → Ker(ĥ)) is divisible.
items.note: Elementary, but not in either library in this form.

items.name: Propositions 7.4–7.5 and Lemma 7.6: the reduction steps
items.statement: (7.4) If f_*ẑ_A comes from P̂ic(C), then for any n > 0, ẑ_A = z_A + n(ẑ + ξ̂_A) with z_A ∈ CH_{0,A}(X), ẑ ∈ ĈH_0(X), f_*ξ̂_A = 0 and f_*z_A coming from Pic(C). (7.5) Such z_A decomposes as z^eff_A + z + ξ_A, with z^eff_A effective reduced of some class y, z ∈ CH_0(X), f_*ξ_A = 0, ξ_A = 0 at S, and curves Z_v with deg(y) ≥ Φ(g_v, d_v). (7.6) Under the hypotheses of Theorem 7.1, Ker(CH_{0,A}(X) → Pic_A(C)) → CH_{0,A}(X)/n is injective for some n, and Ker(ĈH_{0,A}(X) → P̂ic_A(C)) has finite exponent.
items.note: Uses the projection formula f_*(f^*y·[Z]) = dy (item 50) and Mattuck's finiteness (item 49).

items.name: Mattuck: torsion in Pic of a curve over a local field
items.statement: For a finite extension K/Q_p and an abelian variety A/K, Mattuck gives an open subgroup of A(K) isomorphic to the additive group O_K^dim(A). Compactness gives finite index; since the subgroup is torsion-free, A(K)_tors is finite. For a smooth proper geometrically integral curve C/K, Pic⁰(C) embeds in Jac(C)(K), so its torsion is finite. Every torsion class of Pic(C) has degree zero, hence Pic(C)_tors is finite and has finite exponent.
items.note: Finite exponent of Pic torsion is a consequence of Mattuck, not an equivalent formulation. No surjectivity of Pic(C)→Z or equality Pic⁰(C)=Jac(C)(K) without the descent hypothesis is assumed.

items.name: Projection formula and birational invariance of CH_0
items.statement: (a) For f : X → C, a curve Z ⊂ X dominating C with d = [k(Z):k(C)] and y ∈ Pic(C), f_*(f^*y·[Z]) = d·y. (b) CH_0, A₀, Br and H¹(−, Q/Z) are birational invariants of smooth proper varieties in characteristic 0.
items.locator: proof of Proposition 7.4, p. 23; proof of Proposition 8.7, p. 29
items.note: SF.5 plans Chow groups with proper pushforward and the projection formula. The birational invariance of CH_0 (Fulton, Example 16.1.11) is a consequence it should state. The Br and H¹ invariance belong to SF.2.

items.name: Condition 8.1 and Lemma 8.2
items.statement: Condition 8.1 for a smooth proper V over k: the image of ĈH_0(V) in ĈH_{0,A}(V) contains the image of V(A_k)^{Br(V)}. It holds if V satisfies (E), and (Lemma 8.2) if V(k) is dense in V(A_k)^{Br(V)} and V is rationally connected.
items.note: HW20's items 120 and 137 are the same statements, routed to the same Part II. Lemma 8.2 uses [Wit12, Lemme 1.8] and that A₀(V⊗k_v) vanishes at almost all v and has finite exponent everywhere (Kollár–Szabó).

items.name: Theorem 8.3(1): fibrations over curves satisfying (E)
items.statement: Let k be a number field, C a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve, X a smooth proper irreducible k-variety, and f:X→C dominant. Assume the geometric generic fibre is irreducible, H¹(X_ηbar,Q/Z)=0, and A₀(X_ηbar⊗K)=0, where K is an algebraic closure of its function field. If C satisfies (E) and every smooth fibre above a closed point of a Hilbert subset satisfies (E), then X satisfies (E).

items.name: Theorem 8.3(2): the relative exact sequence
items.statement: Let k be a number field, C a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve, X a smooth proper irreducible k-variety, and f:X→C dominant. Assume the geometric generic fibre is irreducible, H¹(X_ηbar,Q/Z)=0, and A₀(X_ηbar⊗K)=0, where K is an algebraic closure of its function field. Under the hypotheses of Theorem 8.3, if the smooth fibers above the closed points of a Hilbert subset of C satisfy (E), then CH_0(X/C) → CH_{0,A}(X/C) → Hom(Br(X)/f^*Br(C), Q/Z) is exact, where CH_0(X/C) and CH_{0,A}(X/C) are the kernels of f_*.
items.note: Uses the injectivity of P̂ic(C) → P̂ic_A(C) [Wit12, Remarques 1.1(v)] and Mordell–Weil for Pic(C).

items.name: Theorem 8.3(3): Condition 8.1 suffices when fibers have multiplicity-one components
items.statement: Let k be a number field, C a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve, X a smooth proper irreducible k-variety, and f:X→C dominant. Assume the geometric generic fibre is irreducible, H¹(X_ηbar,Q/Z)=0, and A₀(X_ηbar⊗K)=0, where K is an algebraic closure of its function field. If every fiber of f has an irreducible component of multiplicity 1, then (1) and (2) of Theorem 8.3 hold when the smooth fibers above closed points of a Hilbert subset only satisfy Condition 8.1.
items.note: HW20's item 121 uses this statement.

items.name: Theorem 8.3(4): (E₁) for the total space
items.statement: Let k be a number field, C a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve, X a smooth proper irreducible k-variety, and f:X→C dominant. Assume the geometric generic fibre is irreducible, H¹(X_ηbar,Q/Z)=0, and A₀(X_ηbar⊗K)=0, where K is an algebraic closure of its function field. If there is (z_v) ∈ Z_{0,A}(X) orthogonal to Br(X) with deg(z_v) = 1 for all v and the class of (f_*z_v) in P̂ic_A(C) in the image of P̂ic(C), and the smooth fibers above the closed points of a Hilbert subset satisfy (E₁), then X has a zero-cycle of degree 1.

items.name: Saito's theorem: curves with trivial divisible Sha satisfy (E)
items.statement: A smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve C over a number field satisfies (E) if the divisible subgroup of the Tate–Shafarevich group of its Jacobian is trivial; if C(k) ≠ ∅ this is equivalent. In particular P^1_k satisfies (E).
items.locator: §1, p. 3, and after Theorem 8.3, p. 27, citing [Sai89], [Wit12, Remarques 1.1(iv)], [Mil86, I.6.26(b)]

items.name: Corollary 8.4: bases birational to P^n, C or P^n × C
items.statement: Let X be smooth proper irreducible over k, Y irreducible and birational to P^n, C or P^n × C (n ≥ 1, C satisfying (E)), and f : X → Y with X_η̄ irreducible, H¹(X_η̄, Q/Z) = 0 and A₀(X_η̄⊗K) = 0. (1) If the smooth fibers above the closed points of a Hilbert subset of Y satisfy (E), X satisfies (E). (2) The same conclusion holds if they only satisfy Condition 8.1 and the fibers above codimension-1 points have a component of multiplicity 1.
items.note: HW20's item 78 cites Corollary 8.4(1). The proof is an induction via Lemmas 8.9, 8.10 and 8.12. Independent review: Here k is a number field and C is a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve satisfying(E). K denotes an algebraic closure of the geometric generic fibre’s function field. Keep the codimension-one component condition for part(2).

items.name: Corollary 8.5: homogeneous-space fibrations satisfy (E)
items.statement: Under the base hypotheses of Corollary 8.4, if f : X → Y is dominant with generic fiber birational to a homogeneous space of a connected linear group with connected geometric stabilisers, then X satisfies (E). Applied to V × P^1 → P^1, this recovers Liang's theorem that such V satisfy (E). It covers fibrations into toric varieties, Châtelet surfaces and p-folds, and del Pezzo surfaces of degree 6.
items.locator: Corollary 8.5, p. 27, and the discussion after it, pp. 27–28
items.note: Uses Borovoi's theorem (item 59), Lemma 8.2 and Corollary 8.4(2), with Graber–Harris–Starr for multiplicity-one components.

items.name: Borovoi's theorem (and Sansuc's for tori)
items.statement: For a smooth compactification X of a homogeneous space of a connected linear algebraic group with connected geometric stabilisers over a number field, X(k) is dense in X(A_k)^{Br(X)} (Borovoi, Corollary 2.5). For torsors under tori this is Sansuc's theorem.
items.locator: proof of Corollary 8.5, p. 27; Corollary 9.29; Remark 9.26
items.note: HW20's candidate HeightsRationalPointsPartIIHomogeneousMassey imports Bor96's connected-stabiliser theorem ('the shared homogeneous owner'), so this item is routed there too, to keep one owner.

items.name: Lemma 8.6: implications between the geometric hypotheses
items.statement: For the geometric generic fiber X_η̄: (a) rationally connected ⇒ (b) A₀(X_η̄⊗K) = 0 ⇒ (c) H^i(X_η, 𝒪) = 0 for i > 0 ⇒ (d) H²(X_η, 𝒪) = 0 ⇒ (e) if H¹(X_η̄, Q/Z) = 0 then Br(X_η)/f_η^*Br(η) is finite; and (c) ⇒ (f) the gcd of the multiplicities of the components of each fiber is 1. Also (a) ⇒ H¹(X_η̄, Q/Z) = 0.
items.locator: Lemma 8.6, p. 28, and the paragraph before Corollary 8.5, p. 27
items.note: HW20's items 11, 17, 135 and 136 (rational connectedness and its geometric vanishing consequences) are in the same Part II. The (b)⇒(c) step uses the decomposition of the diagonal (item 65). Independent review: Use the characteristic-zero smooth proper geometric generic fibre of the stated fibration. Rational connectedness itself and the degree-zero Chow carrier need separate definition/API rows, not only a chain of implications.

items.name: Proposition 8.7: the common statement
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 8.3, for a Hilbert subset H ⊆ C and ẑ_A ∈ ĈH_{0,A}(X) orthogonal to Br(X) with f_*ẑ_A from P̂ic(C), there are ẑ ∈ ĈH_0(X), a closed point c ∈ H and z′_A ∈ Z_{0,A}(X_c) orthogonal to Br(X_c) with f_*z′_A = c and ẑ_A = z′_A + ẑ. The z′_A can be taken effective if every fiber has a multiplicity-one component.
items.note: Combines Theorem 7.1 (with Φ(g, d) = deg(M)d + 2g + 2), Proposition 4.1 and Theorem 6.2, after Chow's lemma and Hironaka.

items.name: Chow's lemma and resolution of singularities in characteristic 0
items.statement: Every proper variety over a field of characteristic 0 is dominated by a smooth projective variety via a birational morphism.
items.note: SF.4 owns resolution in named proved settings (characteristic 0 here). HW20 and HW23 route compactification and resolution there.

items.name: Multiplicity-one components are birational invariants of fibrations
items.statement: For proper regular models over a characteristic-zero discrete valuation ring of birational smooth proper varieties over its fraction field, the existence of a multiplicity-one irreducible component in the special fibre is invariant under the birational comparison (with the residue-field condition retained when asking for a split component). Apply this in the codimension-one fibration setting of Proposition8.7.
items.note: The proper regular model hypotheses are essential to the valuation argument. The original CT11 Proposition3.1 supplier remains to be extracted; an arbitrary birational map of arbitrary schemes is not the asserted interface.

items.name: Lemmas 8.9–8.10: property (∗) in the induction
items.statement: Definition 8.8: a proper variety V over an algebraically closed field satisfies (∗) if it is integral, H¹(V, Q/Z) = 0 and A₀(V⊗K) = 0. (8.9) For g : X → C the composite of f : X → P^n × C with the projection, the geometric generic fiber of g satisfies (∗). The proof uses Raynaud's surjectivity of π₁ onto fibers over codimension-1 points without multiple fibers, purity for H¹ on P^n minus codimension 2, and Leray. (8.10) There is a dense open C⁰ ⊆ C such that for c ∈ C⁰ the geometric generic fiber of f_c : X_c → P^n satisfies (∗). The proof spreads out a decomposition of the diagonal.

items.name: Lemma 8.11 (Bloch–Srinivas): decomposition of the diagonal
items.statement: For the smooth projective geometrically integral varieties used here, let V/k have dimension d, let v be a closed point, and let K be an algebraic closure of k(V). Then A₀(V_K)=0 iff some positive multiple NΔ decomposes in CH_d(V×V) as Γ₁+Γ₂, with Γ₁ supported on V×{v} and Γ₂ on D×V for a proper closed D. The source prints a broader arbitrary-variety statement without properness; see E3.
items.note: This deliberately retains the safe smooth-projective application range. Original Bloch/Srinivas supplier acquisition is still required, especially before claiming a singular or arbitrary-characteristic extension. Properness alone is not advertised as a complete proof repair for that broader range.

items.name: Lemma 8.12: Hilbert subsets of a product
items.statement: For geometrically irreducible V₁, V₂ over a number field and a Hilbert subset H ⊆ V₁ × V₂, there is a Hilbert subset H₂ ⊆ V₂ such that for every h ∈ H₂, H ∩ (V₁ × {h}) contains a Hilbert subset of V₁ × {h}.
items.note: A Hilbert-irreducibility statement for IG.2, in the same direction as HW20's source route for pullbacks of Hilbert subsets.

items.name: Graber–Harris–Starr and consequences
items.statement: A rationally connected fibration over a curve over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 has a section. Hence every fiber over a codimension-1 point of the base of a morphism with rationally connected geometric generic fiber has a component of multiplicity 1, and a variety dominating a rationally connected base with rationally connected generic fiber is rationally connected (GHS, Corollary 1.3). Also H¹(X, Q/Z) = 0 for rationally connected X (Debarre, Corollary 4.18(b)).
items.locator: discussion before Corollary 8.5, p. 27; proof of Corollary 9.25, p. 48
items.note: HW20's items 13 and 132 are in the same Part II. Independent review: Use the smooth projective, geometrically rationally connected characteristic-zero fibre setting of GHS for the section theorem, and the corresponding proper-family setup for its total-space and codimension-one component consequences. These are distinct imported results, not a theorem for arbitrary nonproper morphisms.

items.name: Conjecture 9.1: locally split values of polynomials
items.statement: Let k be a number field, P_1, …, P_n ∈ k[t] pairwise distinct irreducible monic polynomials, k_i = k[t]/(P_i), a_i the class of t, L_i/k_i finite extensions, b_i ∈ k_i^*. Let S be a finite set of places containing the real places and the finite places above which some b_i is not a unit or some L_i/k_i is ramified, and let t_v ∈ k_v (v ∈ S). Assume that for all i and v ∈ S, b_i(t_v − a_i) is a norm from (L_i⊗k_v)^*. Then there is t₀ ∈ k with (1) t₀ arbitrarily close to t_v for v ∈ S, and (2) for every i and every finite place w of k_i with w(t₀ − a_i) > 0, either w lies above S or L_i has a place of degree 1 over w.
items.note: A conjecture, with Remarks 9.3 (reformulation for a common Galois L; reductions to t_v = 0 and to k = Q; enlarging S freely). HW20 (unreviewed) routed its item 76, this conjecture, to HeightsRationalPointsPartIIHomogeneousMassey. The report proposes a single owner.

items.name: Conjecture 9.2: the weak variant
items.statement: As Conjecture 9.1 but with (1) replaced by (1′): t₀ is arbitrarily close to t_v for finite v ∈ S, and at every real place v, for every i and real place w of k_i above v, the sign of (t₀ − a_i)(t_v − a_i) at w is independent of w and i.
items.note: Enough for existence of rational points and for approximation up to connected components at the real places.

items.name: Remarks 9.3: reductions for Conjecture 9.1
items.statement: (i) For a common Galois L, (2) says P_i(t₀) has nonpositive valuation outside S except at places split in L. (ii) One may assume t_v = 0 for v ∈ S and a_i ≠ 0, and Conjectures 9.1–9.2 over Q imply them over every number field. (iii) Finitely many places may be added to S: at a finite v ∉ S, any t_v of valuation −N∏[L_i:k_i] (N large) satisfies the local hypothesis.
items.note: (ii) is only sketched ('compare [CTSD94, Proposition 4.1]'). The design should write out the reduction to Q, e.g. by taking L_i^0 the Galois closure of L_i over Q(a_i) and b_i^0 = −a_i^{-1}.

items.name: Definition 9.4: almost abelian extensions
items.statement: A finite extension L/k of characteristic-zero fields is almost abelian if it is abelian, or if for some prime p there is a bijection Spec(L⊗_k k̄) ≅ 𝔽_p under which Gal(k̄/k) acts by affine transformations x ↦ ax + b. Examples 9.5: cubic extensions, and k(c^{1/p})/k.
items.apiStatus: open: consumer-derived planning API and three discriminating tests required; see G2

items.name: Schinzel's hypothesis (H), its homogeneous variant (HH₁), and (H) ⇒ (HH₁)
items.statement: (H): for irreducible P_1, …, P_n ∈ ℤ[t] with positive leading coefficients and no fixed prime divisor of ∏P_i, there are infinitely many t with all P_i(t) prime. (HH₁) over a number field k: for irreducible homogeneous P_1, …, P_n ∈ k[λ, μ] and S large enough, given (λ_v, μ_v) at v ∈ S there is (λ₀, μ₀) close at finite places, projectively close at archimedean ones, positive at real ones, integral outside S, with each P_i(λ₀, μ₀) a unit outside S except at one place where it is a uniformiser. (H) implies (HH₁) (Swinnerton-Dyer, Lemma 7.1).
items.note: Conjectural statements. RS-07 moved the prime-tuple conjecture register to SV.4, so Schinzel's generalisation is registered there too. SkorobogatovSofos23's candidate ArithmeticStatisticsPartIISchinzelAverages proves an averaged form. Independent review: SV.4 is the Maynard bounded-gaps layer, not the prime-tuples conjecture register. AN.6 owns that register. Split the conjectural predicates from the proved H⇒HH1 reduction, with exact local admissibility, nonvanishing and real positivity conditions acquired from the original supplier.

items.name: Theorem 9.6: Schinzel's hypothesis implies Conjecture 9.1 for almost abelian extensions
items.statement: Assume (H). If L_1/k_1, …, L_n/k_n are almost abelian, Conjecture 9.1 holds. Lemma 9.8: for non-abelian almost abelian L_j/k_j there is a nontrivial cyclic E_j/k_j in the Galois closure such that every place unramified in L_j either splits completely in E_j or has a degree-1 place of L_j above it.
items.note: The proof adds places inert in E_j to make Σ_S inv(E_j/k_j, t_v − a_j) ≠ 0, applies (HH₁), and uses global reciprocity for the abelian L_i and E_j. Its inputs are Chebotarev and the Artin–Tate corollary (item 74).

items.name: Global reciprocity for norms from abelian extensions
items.statement: For a finite abelian extension L/k of number fields and a∈k×, if a is a local norm at every place except possibly one, it is a local norm at that last place. Apply the global sum of invariants separately to every character of Gal(L/k), and the local norm criterion; one selected cyclic character is not an equivalent test for a general noncyclic abelian extension.
items.note: Tau Ceti Class Field Theory plans the sum of local invariants (Layer 10) and the norm theorems (Layer 13).

items.name: Remark 9.7: Heath-Brown–Moroz primes of binary cubic forms give (HH₁) in degree 3
items.statement: From Heath-Brown and Moroz's theorem on primes represented by binary cubic forms, (HH₁) holds for k = Q, n = 1, deg P_1 = 3. Hence Conjecture 9.1 holds for n = 1, k = Q, [k_1:Q] = 3 and L_1/k_1 almost abelian.
items.note: The analytic input is a prime-detecting sieve for binary cubic forms (Heath-Brown's method), in the direction of SV.5's separate advanced-sieve developments.

items.name: The variety W of §9.2.2 and Proposition 9.9
items.statement: W is the fiber over 0 of (A² ∖ {0}) × ∏_i (R_{L_i/k}(A¹) ∖ F_i) → ∏_i R_{k_i/k}(A¹), (λ, μ, x) ↦ (b_i(λ − a_iμ) − N_{L_i/k_i}(x_i))_i, with p : W → P^1 the projection. Proposition 9.9: Conjecture 9.1 holds for all S, (t_v) if and only if ∪_{c∈P^1(k)} W_c(A_k) is dense in W(A_k). Its converse direction uses Theorem 9.17 with B = 0 and Br_vert(W/P^1) = image(Br(k)→Br(W)).
items.note: The vertical Brauer computation uses the Faddeev description of Br(k(t)) and the residues of CT–SwD (Propositions 1.1.1, 1.2.1).
items.apiStatus: open: consumer-derived planning API and three discriminating tests required; see G2

items.name: Corollary 9.10: strong approximation for W implies Conjecture 9.1
items.statement: If W satisfies strong approximation off every finite place, then Conjecture 9.1 holds for the given data.

items.name: Theorem 9.11: Conjecture 9.1 in small degree
items.statement: Conjecture 9.1 holds if (i) Σ_i [k_i:k] ≤ 2, or (ii) Σ_i [k_i:k] = 3 and [L_i:k_i] = 2 for all i.
items.note: (i): W is affine space minus codimension 2 (Lemma 1.8). (ii): W is a punctured cone over a smooth 4-dimensional quadric minus codimension 2. Strong approximation for such quadric complements goes by conics, then [CTX11, Proposition 3.1] for the cone.

items.name: Lemma 9.13: invariance under Möbius changes of coordinates
items.statement: Given α, β, γ, δ ∈ k with αδ − βγ ≠ 0, γa_i + δ ≠ 0, γt_v + δ ≠ 0, α and αa_i + β units outside S, and (αδ − βγ)/(γt_v + δ) a local norm at S, Conjectures 9.1–9.2 for (a_i, b_i, S, t_v) reduce to the same conjectures for a′_i = (αa_i + β)/(γa_i + δ), b′_i = b_i(γa_i + δ), S′ ⊇ S′₀ and t′_v. The key identity is b′_i(t′₀ − a′_i) = b_i(t₀ − a_i)(α − γt′₀).
items.note: The proof of (4) contains a misprint ('lies above' for 'does not lie above'; sourceIssue E1). The identity was checked. Independent review: E1 corrects the proof’s S′ complement, not the statement or the Möbius identity. Separate the four transport conclusions when this bundle is decomposed.

items.name: Matthiesen's theorem on norm-form values of linear forms
items.statement: Let f_i(λ, μ) = b_i(λ − a_iμ) ∈ ℤ[λ, μ] be pairwise non-proportional linear forms and L_i/Q number fields, and S a large finite set of primes. For (λ₁, μ₁) ∈ ℤ² at which each f_i is a local integral norm from L_i at the primes of S and a real norm, there are (λ₀, μ₀) ∈ ℤ² arbitrarily close to it at S (and projectively at ∞) with each f_i(λ₀, μ₀) squarefree outside S and the norm of an integral element of L_i.
items.note: Proved by Green–Tao linear-patterns methods for the representation function of norm forms (Matthiesen, building on Browning–Matthiesen). AC.5 owns finite-complexity linear patterns and nilsequence orthogonality. Independent review: The norm-form theorem is only paraphrased here. Exact integral admissibility, complexity, archimedean region and square-free representation-function hypotheses from Matthiesen remain missing; route8 is rejected until supplied.

items.name: Theorem 9.14: Conjecture 9.1 when k = k_1 = ⋯ = k_n = Q
items.statement: Conjecture 9.1 holds when k = k_1 = ⋯ = k_n = Q, i.e. for products of linear polynomials over Q with arbitrary L_i.
items.note: Deduced from Matthiesen's theorem (item 80) via Lemma 9.13 with (α, β, γ, δ) = (r^{2N}, 0, 0, r^N), and strong approximation to make (λ₁, μ₁) integral.

items.name: Irving's sieve theorem for binary cubic forms
items.statement: For a binary cubic form f ∈ ℤ[x, y] (positive x³ coefficient, negative real roots, from a cubic field K with one real place not embedding in Q(ζ_q), q ≥ 7 prime) and suitable local data at S, there are positive integers (x₀, y₀) arbitrarily close to (λ, μ) at S such that y₀f(x₀, y₀) has no prime factor p ∉ S with p ≡ 1 (mod q).
items.note: A lower-bound sieve result with a restricted set of prime factors, in the direction of SV.5. Independent review: The phrase suitable local data is an unresolved hypothesis, not an exact supplier theorem. Read Irving §§3–6 and extract the sieve lower bound and its congruence restrictions before building from route7.

items.name: Theorem 9.15 (after Irving): a cubic case of Conjecture 9.2
items.statement: Let K/Q be cubic with a unique real place, not embedding into Q(ζ_q), q ≥ 7 prime. Then Conjecture 9.2 holds for n = 2, k = Q, k_1 = K, L_1 = K(2^{1/q}), k_2 = Q, L_2 = Q(2^{1/q}). Lemma 9.16: by a change of coordinates one may assume b_2t_∞ < b_2a_1 < b_2a_2 at the real place of K.
items.note: It is the first known case with Σ[k_i:k] ≥ 4 and k_i ≠ k. The sign bookkeeping of Lemma 9.16 was checked. The main result of Irving on N_{K/Q}(x) = P(t) for cubic P is recovered.

items.name: Theorem 9.17: the main theorem on rational points in fibrations over P^1
items.statement: Let X be smooth irreducible over a number field k and f : X → P^1_k with geometrically irreducible generic fiber and a multiplicity-one component in every fiber. Let U ⊆ P^1_k be dense open with split fibers and ∞ ∈ U, B ⊆ Br(f^{-1}(U)) finite, and (x_v) ∈ X(A_k) orthogonal to (B + f_η^*Br(η)) ∩ Br(X). Let M′ ⊆ P^1 ∖ U be nonempty, containing all non-split points, such that for each m ∈ M″ = (P^1 ∖ U) ∖ M′ the residue map Br(P^1 ∖ (M′ ∪ {m})) → H¹(k(m), Q/Z) is onto. Assume Conjecture 9.1 for the P_i vanishing on M′ (resp. Conjecture 9.2, with either M″ = ∅ and f proper or k totally imaginary). Then there are c ∈ U(k) with X_c smooth and (x′_v) ∈ X_c(A_k) orthogonal to B and arbitrarily close to (x_v) in X(A_k) (resp. in X(A_k)_•).
items.locator: Theorem 9.17, p. 42; proof with Lemmas 9.19–9.20, pp. 43–46
items.note: Uses Pic₊(P^1) and Theorem 2.5, Harari's formal lemma and evaluation formula (item 21), Weil reciprocity (Lemma 9.19), Harari's Frobenius argument for the fibers over M″ (Lemma 9.20), Chebotarev, and Ekedahl's geometric Chebotarev. The Remarks 9.18 surjectivity statement uses the Faddeev sequence and the surjectivity of corestriction for totally imaginary fields. Independent review: E4 refutes the printed flat+proper real-openness step in the weak-Conjecture9.2 real case. It is a proof gate, not a disproof of Theorem9.17. Strong Conjecture9.1 and the totally imaginary alternative avoid this particular step. Simply shrinking U to the smooth locus changes the polynomial/sign data in the restricted conjectural hypothesis.

items.name: Adelic points modulo connected components at infinity
items.statement: For a proper variety V over a number field, V(A_k)_• = ∏_{v∈Ω_f} V(k_v) × ∏_{v∈Ω_∞} π₀(V(k_v)) (Poonen's notation, after Stoll).
items.note: A variant of RP.2's adelic point space.
items.apiStatus: open: consumer-derived planning API and three discriminating tests required; see G2

items.name: Weil reciprocity on a proper regular curve
items.statement: For rational functions f,g on a proper regular geometrically integral curve over the characteristic-zero field used here, the product over all closed points of the norms of their tame symbols is1. For disjoint divisors this yields f(div g)=g(div f). On P¹ the point at infinity is included.
items.locator: proof of Lemma 9.19, p. 43; Remarks 9.18(ii) and proof of Proposition 9.9, pp. 37 and 42
items.note: The Brauer Faddeev sequence was bundled with this K-theoretic reciprocity target; it is now the separate corrected item104 in SF.2. The original affine-indexed five-term sequence was false.

items.name: Surjectivity of corestriction on H¹(−, Q/Z) for totally imaginary fields
items.statement: For a finite extension k′/k of totally imaginary number fields, Cores : H¹(k′, Q/Z) → H¹(k, Q/Z) is surjective (dual to injectivity of C_k/D_k → C_{k′}/D_{k′}; Gras, Note p. 327).
items.note: A class field theory statement not named in the Tau Ceti Class Field Theory layers. It is recorded with the fibration Part II, which uses it. Independent review: Generic class-field corestriction is removed from the private fibration owner and proposed as a ClassFieldTheory continuation, route15. Original Gras p327 and the topology of the divisible idele-class quotient remain unexpanded.

items.name: Ekedahl's geometric Chebotarev density theorem
items.statement: In the good-model situation of Theorem9.17, a finite étale Galois cover with its field of constants separated has, at sufficiently large residue fields, rational points whose Frobenius represents any conjugacy class compatible with arithmetic Frobenius on the constants. In the application at a prime completely split in L_i, this realizes each element of H_i=Gal(E_i/K_i k(Y_i)) on the selected fibre. One cannot demand every element of the full arithmetic group at an arbitrary prime.
items.note: The constant-field restriction and uniform good-model bound are explicit. WC.5 supplies point-count estimates, but the general quasi-projective/uniform Chebotarev adapter still needs original Ekedahl/Lang–Weil sources and a layer contract.

items.name: Theorem 9.22: Theorem 9.17 with c in a Hilbert subset
items.statement: Under the notation and assumptions of Theorem 9.17, for any Hilbert subset H ⊆ P^1_k, the point c ∈ U(k) can be required to lie in H.
items.note: The printed proof asserts that elements of B₀ ⊂ Br(X) evaluate trivially on X(k_v) for almost all v. That is false for the non-proper X the theorem allows, and integral points repair it (sourceIssue E2). Independent review: E2 supplies integral outside-S choices and a finite auxiliary approximation set from Smeets Proposition6.1. E4 remains the separate real-topology proof gate inherited from9.17; repairing integrality alone does not close that branch.

items.name: Corollary 9.23: the conditional fibration theorem over P^1
items.statement: Let X be smooth proper irreducible over k and f : X → P^1_k with X_η̄ irreducible. Assume (1) H¹(X_η̄, Q/Z) = 0 and H²(X_η̄, 𝒪) = 0; (2) every fiber has a multiplicity-one component; (3) Conjecture 9.1 (resp. 9.2); (4) X_c(k) dense in X_c(A_k)^{Br(X_c)} (resp. in X_c(A_k)^{Br(X_c)}_•) for every rational point c of a Hilbert subset. Then X(k) is dense in X(A_k)^{Br(X)} (resp. X(A_k)^{Br(X)}_•).
items.note: Independent review: All statements here retain the paper’s number-field ground field and smooth proper irreducible total-space hypotheses. Hypotheses referenced from9.23 or8.4 must be imported in full when the bundled targets are split.

items.name: Corollary 9.24: Conjecture 9.1 only for the non-split points
items.statement: With (1), (2) and (4) of Corollary 9.23 and f^{-1}(∞) split, let M′ ⊂ A¹_k be finite containing the non-split points, containing a rational point unless k is totally imaginary. If Conjecture 9.1 holds for the polynomials vanishing on M′, then X(k) is dense in X(A_k)^{Br(X)}.
items.note: Independent review: All statements here retain the paper’s number-field ground field and smooth proper irreducible total-space hypotheses. Hypotheses referenced from9.23 or8.4 must be imported in full when the bundled targets are split.

items.name: Corollary 9.25: rationally connected fibrations over P^n
items.statement: Let n ≥ 1, X smooth proper irreducible over k, and f : X → P^n_k dominant with rationally connected geometric generic fiber. Assume Conjecture 9.1 (resp. 9.2). If X_c(k) is dense in X_c(A_k)^{Br(X_c)} (resp. •) for every rational point c of a Hilbert subset of P^n_k, then X(k) is dense in X(A_k)^{Br(X)} (resp. •).
items.note: HW20's item 77 cites this corollary (and HW20's Theorem 6.1 uses it). The proof is an induction via P^n ~ P^{n−1} × P^1, Lemma 8.12, Graber–Harris–Starr and finiteness of Br(X)/Br(k). Independent review: All statements here retain the paper’s number-field ground field and smooth proper irreducible total-space hypotheses. Hypotheses referenced from9.23 or8.4 must be imported in full when the bundled targets are split.

items.name: Corollary 9.27: the conditional theorem under Schinzel's hypothesis
items.statement: In the paper’s setup, k is a number field, X is smooth proper irreducible, and f:X→P¹_k is dominant with geometrically irreducible generic fibre. Assume (H). Let f : X → P^1_k have geometrically irreducible generic fiber, with every fiber containing a multiplicity-one component whose function field has an almost abelian algebraic closure of k(m). If the fibers above the rational points of a Hilbert subset satisfy weak approximation, then X(k) is dense in X(A_k)^{Br_vert(X/P^1)}.
items.note: Extends Colliot-Thélène–Skorobogatov–Swinnerton-Dyer [CTSSD98, §1] and recovers Wei [Wei14a, Theorem 3.5]. Independent review: All statements here retain the paper’s number-field ground field and smooth proper irreducible total-space hypotheses. Hypotheses referenced from9.23 or8.4 must be imported in full when the bundled targets are split.

items.name: Theorem 9.28: the unconditional theorem over Q
items.statement: Let X be smooth proper irreducible over Q and f : X → P^1_Q dominant with rationally connected geometric generic fiber, whose non-split fibers lie over rational points. If X_c(Q) is dense in X_c(A_Q)^{Br(X_c)} for every rational point c of a Hilbert subset, then X(Q) is dense in X(A_Q)^{Br(X)}.
items.note: Corollary 9.24 together with Theorem 9.14. Independent review: All statements here retain the paper’s number-field ground field and smooth proper irreducible total-space hypotheses. Hypotheses referenced from9.23 or8.4 must be imported in full when the bundled targets are split.

items.name: Corollary 9.29 and Remark 9.30: pencils of homogeneous spaces over Q
items.statement: If X is smooth proper irreducible over Q with f : X → P^1_Q whose generic fiber is birational to a homogeneous space of a connected linear group with connected geometric stabilisers, and the non-split fibers lie over rational points, then X(Q) is dense in X(A_Q)^{Br(X)}. The same holds over P^n_Q if the non-split codimension-1 fibers lie over generic points of hyperplanes defined over Q.
items.note: Subsumes Browning–Matthiesen, Browning–Matthiesen–Skorobogatov, HSW §4, Smeets §3.2 and Skorobogatov 2015. Independent review: All statements here retain the paper’s number-field ground field and smooth proper irreducible total-space hypotheses. Hypotheses referenced from9.23 or8.4 must be imported in full when the bundled targets are split.

items.name: Theorem 9.31: fibrations of rank at most 2
items.statement: In the paper’s setup, k is a number field, X is smooth proper irreducible, and f:X→P¹_k is dominant with geometrically irreducible generic fibre. Let f : X → P^1_k be dominant with rationally connected geometric generic fiber, rank(f) ≤ 2 (the sum of the degrees of the points with non-split fiber), and either k totally imaginary or the non-split fibers over rational points. If X_c(k) is dense in X_c(A_k)^{Br(X_c)} for every rational point c of a Hilbert subset, then X(k) is dense in X(A_k)^{Br(X)}.
items.note: Corollary 9.24 with Theorem 9.11(i). A footnote added in proof says the 'totally imaginary or rational points' hypothesis is superfluous, with details to appear elsewhere. The atlas should keep the printed hypothesis until that proof is sourced. Independent review: All statements here retain the paper’s number-field ground field and smooth proper irreducible total-space hypotheses. Hypotheses referenced from9.23 or8.4 must be imported in full when the bundled targets are split.

items.name: Remark 9.26: fibrations into torsors under tori
items.statement: In the paper’s setup, k is a number field, X is smooth proper irreducible, and f:X→P¹_k is dominant with geometrically irreducible generic fibre. If the generic fiber of f : X → P^1_k is birational to a torsor under a torus over k(t), then hypotheses (1), (2), (4) of Corollary 9.23 hold (Sansuc for (4)), so X(k) is dense in X(A_k)^{Br(X)} as soon as the varieties W of §9.2.2 satisfy strong approximation off every finite place.
items.note: Compare Skorobogatov 2015, Theorem 1.1 (constant torus, weak approximation on W). Independent review: All statements here retain the paper’s number-field ground field and smooth proper irreducible total-space hypotheses. Hypotheses referenced from9.23 or8.4 must be imported in full when the bundled targets are split.

items.name: Chebotarev's density theorem
items.statement: For a finite Galois extension of number fields, every conjugacy class of the Galois group is the Frobenius of a set of primes of positive Dirichlet density. In particular infinitely many primes split completely, and in an abelian extension such as HK/k every class of the Artin map is attained.
items.note: Tau Ceti Chebotarev plans abelian and Dirichlet-density Chebotarev. Its audit records the construction as unfinished.

items.name: Weak approximation at finite sets of number-field places
items.statement: For a number field K, finite sets of finite and infinite places, the diagonal K-map into the product of their actual completions has dense range.
items.locator: proof of Lemma 1.8, p. 8; §5.4; proof of Theorem 9.14
items.note: Exact pinned declaration read at Global/Approximation/Weak.lean:202, with Field/NumberField hypotheses. Additive strong approximation off one arbitrary place is separated as102; upstream Layer6 states only density in the finite adeles.

items.name: Smooth-scheme Hensel consequence of algebra lifting
items.statement: For a smooth scheme over a complete discrete valuation ring O, every residue-field point lifts to an O-point. Select an affine neighbourhood of the special point, compare scheme smoothness with formal smoothness of its coordinate algebra, and apply25. The ring theorem is built; this geometric adapter is planned.
items.locator: HW16 uses throughout §§3,5,9; Mathlib algebra theorem25; SF.4 infinitesimal lifting

items.name: Quasi-projective symmetric powers and reduced-image smoothness
items.statement: For a quasi-projective variety X in characteristic zero, construct X^d/S_d as Sym^d(X), compatible with base change and morphisms. For a morphism f:X→C, with C a smooth curve, Sym^d(f) is smooth at a cycle z if f is smooth at its support and f_*z is reduced. For d=0 both spaces are the base point; the paper uses d≥1.
items.locator: Notation author p6 and Lemma5.6 author p18
items.note: Import the existing curve target41; own the general finite-action quotient and its local disjoint-support calculation in SF.1.

planningAPI.name: sym_quotient_universal
planningAPI.statement: For characteristic-zero quasi-projective X, the quotient map X^d→Sym^d X is universal for S_d-invariant morphisms, with the chosen geometric quotient and residue-cycle dictionary.

planningAPI.name: sym_map_comp_base_change
planningAPI.statement: Construct Sym^d(f), prove identity/composition and compatibility with field base change; use the same curve carrier as41 by a specified comparison isomorphism.

planningAPI.name: sym_reduced_image_smooth
planningAPI.statement: If f is smooth at each point supporting z and f_*z is reduced, prove Sym^d(f) smooth at z by passing to disjoint local factors of the quotient.

unitTests.name: degree_zero_and_one
unitTests.statement: Sym^0(X)=Spec k and Sym^1(X)=X, with induced map identities.

unitTests.name: curve_agreement
unitTests.statement: For X=P1, compare the shared curve Sym^d with P^d and its effective degree-d divisor interpretation.

unitTests.name: ramification_is_not_smooth
unitTests.statement: For f:A1→A1, x↦x², at the degree-one cycle[0] the image is reduced but f is ramified; reject smoothness without the support hypothesis.

unitTests.statement: For the smooth projection A2→A1 and d=2 with two distinct image points, the local quotient decomposes into two smooth factors and has relative dimension2.

items.name: Additive strong approximation with one arbitrary place omitted
items.statement: For a number field k and any chosen place v0, k is dense in the restricted product of k_v over v≠v0, with O_v as the distinguished subgroup at finite places. Thus finitely many local approximations away from v0 can be imposed together with integrality at all other finite places. This includes v0 finite, so it is stronger than density in finite adeles.
items.locator: HW16 Lemma1.8 and §5.4, author pp8,18; original additive strong-approximation supplier to acquire
items.note: Import99, the existing number-field/adele carriers and the finite-adele target of GlobalNumberFields Layer6. A new continuation is required for the extra endpoint; do not rewrite upstream.

items.name: Normal-crossings norm boundary after finite étale base change
items.statement: For a finite étale algebra L/k of positive rank n, the complement of Res G_m in Res A¹ becomes the union of n coordinate hyperplanes after a splitting extension. Its singular locus has codimension at least2, and is empty when n=1. For integral models the same statement applies after removing ramified primes, so the base extension is finite étale.
items.note: The rank-one empty locus and the étale integral-base restriction correct the original bundled item40.

items.name: Faddeev residue sequence including infinity
items.statement: For a characteristic-zero field k, the sequence 0→Br(k)→Br(k(t))→⊕_(m∈(P¹_k)^(1)) H¹(k(m),Q/Z)→H¹(k,Q/Z)→0 is exact, with residues followed by sum of corestrictions. Equivalently the affine-only residue sequence 0→Br(k)→Br(k(t))→⊕_(m∈(A¹_k)^(1)) H¹(k(m),Q/Z)→0 ends there.
items.locator: HW16 Proposition9.9 and Remarks9.18(ii), author pp37,42
items.note: The input mistakenly combined the affine index set with the projective final sum map. For (χ,t), residues χ at0 and −χ at∞ exhibit the error. SF.2 owns the cohomological Brauer/localization construction; T.4 is imported for its K-theoretic reciprocity comparison.

items.name: Lemma9.19: the Pic-plus class gives local norms
items.statement: In the notation of the proof of9.17, define b_i by evaluating t−a_i on −c1. Equality of c1 and f(x″_v) in Pic-plus(P¹_kv), together with the L_infinity norm condition, implies b_i(t_v−a_i) is a norm from L_i⊗k k_v to k_i⊗k k_v, for every i and v.

items.name: Lemma9.20: reciprocity forces the Frobenius error into H_i
items.statement: In the proof of9.17, for i>n set σ_i=Σ_(v∈Ω_i minus{v_i}) n_(w,i)Frob_(ξ_(w,i))∈G_i. The auxiliary residue-surjective subgroup Γ_i and global reciprocity make every character of G_i/H_i vanish on σ_i; hence σ_i∈H_i. This permits cancellation by geometric Frobenius realization at v_i.

routes.reason: RP.2 owns adelic point spaces, local invariants and the Brauer–Manin pairing. HW20's routes (not yet reviewed) extend that interface to zero-cycles and to Harari's formal lemma. This paper uses exactly those tools: Manin's cycle pairing through corestriction, Harari's formal lemma, the ramified-evaluation theorem and the fiber-component evaluation formula (Harari 1994, 2.1.1, 2.4.3, 2.6.1), and Stoll's adelic points modulo connected components. They are general Brauer-evaluation tools, not specific to fibrations. The variety-level strong-approximation predicate9 is defined on this owner’s restricted adelic point carrier; it is not a second adelic construction. Harari’s three bundled suppliers still need their exact original hypotheses.

SF.2 owns étale cohomology of schemes. HW20 and HW23 routed its 𝔾_m-cohomology, residue and purity inputs, and the scheme Hochschild–Serre sequence, there. The same belongs there here: Grothendieck's sequence Pic⊗Q/Z → H²(Q/Z(1)) → Br and the finiteness of geometric Br when H²(𝒪) = 0; the residue of a pulled-back class along a fiber component (multiplicity times the restricted residue); and the vanishing of Br for finite 𝒪_v-algebras and complete local rings with finite residue field. Include corrected Faddeev104 with all projective closed points and characteristic-zero Kummer coefficients; keep the cohomological/Azumaya and henselian local-ring bridges explicit.

IG.2 owns Hilbert irreducibility over number fields, which RS-29 kept intact, and HW20's routes already use it for Hilbert subsets of all scheme points. Lemma 6.1 (approximating a closed point of a Hilbert set in the symmetric products at finitely many places keeps one in the Hilbert set, after Swinnerton-Dyer and Smeets) and Lemma 8.12 (Hilbert subsets of products) are statements of that theory. Smeets Proposition6.1 is now read in the correct original paper, arXiv1305.0756 pp14–15; HW16 Lemma6.1 supplies the closed-point extension and8.12 supplies the product Hilbert subset. These belong to IG.2 with finite étale-cover inputs from IG.0.

WC.5 owns point-count bounds over finite fields. The paper repeatedly needs the elementary Lang–Weil–Nisnevich estimate for arbitrary geometrically irreducible varieties, and Ekedahl's geometric Chebotarev for étale covers of families. Both are finite-field counting statements in that direction, weaker in form than, but not implied by, WC.5's cohomological bound for smooth projective varieties. The atlas states neither. WC.5 currently states smooth-projective cohomological point-count bounds. Uniform arbitrary-variety Lang–Weil and geometric Chebotarev with its constant-field coset are new proof obligations; the shared owner is appropriate but this brief is not yet a sufficient build contract.

MC.0 constructs correspondences and their action on Chow groups. The Bloch–Srinivas decomposition of the diagonal, with its converse via divisibility of A₀ over algebraically closed fields, is a correspondence statement used here and in HW20's rational-connectedness inputs. Restrict the supplied theorem to the smooth-projective range in65; E3 records the missing properness in the printed broader wording. Acquire Bloch80/Bloch–Srinivas83 Proposition1 before claiming the broader equivalence.

Register Schinzel(H) and the exact HH1 predicate here as assumptions; the separate proved H⇒HH1 arithmetic reduction still needs its original statement and proof contract, so this bundled source route is not accepted yet.

SV.5 owns advanced sieves and prime-detecting developments as separate source-scoped results. Heath-Brown–Moroz (primes represented by binary cubic forms) and Irving's lower-bound sieve for binary cubic forms with prime factors restricted modulo q are the analytic inputs of Remark 9.7 and Theorem 9.15.

AC.5 owns finite-complexity linear patterns in primes and nilsequence orthogonality. sourceIssues.reason: Assertion (4) says: either w lies above S, or w does not lie above S′ and w(t′₀ − a′_i) > 0. The first case is immediate, and the preceding sentence excludes w above S′ ∖ S. previous.statement: For a smooth proper curve C over a finite extension k_v of Q_p, the torsion subgroup of Pic(C⊗k_v) has finite exponent. Equivalently, the Jacobian has J(k_v) ≅ 𝒪_v^g × finite.

previous.statement: Let C be a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve over a number field k, X smooth proper irreducible, and f : X → C with X_η̄ irreducible, H¹(X_η̄, Q/Z) = 0 and A₀(X_η̄⊗K) = 0. If C satisfies (E) and the smooth fibers of f above the closed points of a Hilbert subset of C satisfy (E), then X satisfies (E).

Under the hypotheses of Theorem 8.3, if the smooth fibers above the closed points of a Hilbert subset of C satisfy (E), then CH_0(X/C) → CH_{0,A}(X/C) → Hom(Br(X)/f^*Br(C), Q/Z) is exact, where CH_0(X/C) and CH_{0,A}(X/C) are the kernels of f_*.
If every fiber of f has an irreducible component of multiplicity 1, then (1) and (2) of Theorem 8.3 hold when the smooth fibers above closed points of a Hilbert subset only satisfy Condition 8.1.

If there is (z_v) ∈ Z_{0,A}(X) orthogonal to Br(X) with deg(z_v) = 1 for all v and the class of (f_*z_v) in P̂ic_A(C) in the image of P̂ic(C), and the smooth fibers above the closed points of a Hilbert subset satisfy (E₁), then X has a zero-cycle of degree 1.

previous.statement: Assume (H). Let f : X → P^1_k have geometrically irreducible generic fiber, with every fiber containing a multiplicity-one component whose function field has an almost abelian algebraic closure of k(m). If the fibers above the rational points of a Hilbert subset satisfy weak approximation, then X(k) is dense in X(A_k)^{Br_vert(X/P^1)}.

Let f : X → P^1_k be dominant with rationally connected geometric generic fiber, rank(f) ≤ 2 (the sum of the degrees of the points with non-split fiber), and either k totally imaginary or the non-split fibers over rational points. If X_c(k) is dense in X_c(A_k)^{Br(X_c)} for every rational point c of a Hilbert subset, then X(k) is dense in X(A_k)^{Br(X)}.

If the generic fiber of f : X → P^1_k is birational to a torsor under a torus over k(t), then hypotheses (1), (2), (4) of Corollary 9.23 hold (Sansuc for (4)), so X(k) is dense in X(A_k)^{Br(X)} as soon as the varieties W of §9.2.2 satisfy strong approximation off every finite place.
